explanation.summary: The rubella rash is maculopapular, begins on the face, spreads to the rest of the body, and typically lasts about 3 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rubella commonly presents with a maculopapular rash, a combination of flat and raised red lesions. The rash usually starts on the face or head and spreads to the rest of the body. Because it typically lasts about 3 days, rubella is sometimes called 3-day measles. Most symptoms resolve in 7 to 10 days.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The rubella rash starts on the face and progresses downward, not upward from the legs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The rubella rash lasts about 3 days rather than persisting for weeks with desquamation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Targetoid palmar and plantar lesions are not a feature of rubella.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vesicles in crops are not the maculopapular eruption described for rubella.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man with confirmed rubella has tender, enlarged lymph nodes on examination. Which of the following nodal groups is characteristically involved in this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anterior cervical and submandibular

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epitrochlear and inguinal

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mediastinal and hilar

choices.label: D
choices.text: Posterior auricular and suboccipital

choices.label: E
choices.text: Supraclavicular and axillary

explanation.summary: Rubella classically produces swollen lymph nodes behind the ears and at the back of the neck.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymphadenopathy in rubella characteristically involves the nodes behind the ears, the posterior auricular nodes, and those at the back of the neck, the suboccipital nodes. The adenopathy can be more generalized, and it is one of the symptoms that may persist after the rash and fever have resolved.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anterior cervical and submandibular nodes are not the groups emphasized in rubella.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epitrochlear and inguinal nodes are not the classic rubella distribution.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intrathoracic adenopathy is not a described feature of rubella.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Supraclavicular and axillary adenopathy is not characteristic of rubella.

questions.stem: Two adults in the same household are diagnosed with rubella: a 29-year-old woman and her 31-year-old husband. The woman develops joint pain and swelling of the wrists and knees, while her husband has only fever, rash, and malaise. Which of the following best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arthralgia and arthritis are much more common in women than in men

choices.label: B
choices.text: Joint disease occurs only in patients vaccinated during childhood

choices.label: C
choices.text: Joint findings appear only after the rash has completely resolved

choices.label: D
choices.text: Joint involvement follows only a second infection with rubella virus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Joint symptoms reflect coinfection with another respiratory virus

explanation.summary: Arthralgia and arthritis are recognized features of rubella and are much more common in women than in men.
explanation.whyCorrect: Along with rash, lymphadenopathy, mild fever, and malaise, rubella commonly causes arthralgia or arthritis. Joint swelling and pain are much more common in women than in men, which is why an affected woman may have prominent joint complaints while an affected man in the same household does not.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Prior vaccination is not a prerequisite for joint involvement; these patients have wild-type infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Joint symptoms occur as part of the acute illness rather than only after the rash clears.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Joint symptoms are part of primary rubella infection and do not require a second exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arthralgia and arthritis are described features of rubella itself, not of a coinfection.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old college student is diagnosed with rubella on the day her rash appeared. The health department asks over what interval she is capable of transmitting the virus to her contacts. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: For 21 days after the rash has fully resolved

choices.label: B
choices.text: From 14 days before the rash until it appears

choices.label: C
choices.text: From 2 days before until 2 days after the rash

choices.label: D
choices.text: From 7 days before until 7 days after rash onset

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only during the days that the rash is visible

explanation.summary: Patients with rubella shed virus from 7 days before to 7 days after rash onset, and are most infectious just before the rash appears.
explanation.whyCorrect: While patients with rubella are most infectious just before the rash appears, they shed the virus for 7 days before and 7 days after rash onset. This wide shedding window, combined with the fact that many rubella infections go unrecognized because they resemble other viral illnesses, makes contact tracing important.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Shedding ends about 7 days after rash onset rather than continuing for weeks afterward.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Shedding does not stop when the rash appears; it continues for another 7 days.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This window is far too narrow on both ends of rash onset.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shedding begins well before the rash is visible and continues after it fades.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old with a maculopapular rash and posterior auricular lymphadenopathy develops headache, confusion, and a generalized seizure. Which of the following complications has most likely occurred, and how often does it complicate rubella?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial meningitis, in roughly 1 in 500 cases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Encephalitis, in roughly 1 in 50 cases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encephalitis, in roughly 1 in 6,000 cases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myocarditis, in roughly 1 in 100 cases

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thrombocytopenic purpura, in roughly 1 in 10 cases

explanation.summary: Encephalitis complicates roughly 1 in 6,000 rubella infections and can cause headache, confusion, seizures, coma, and death.
explanation.whyCorrect: Encephalitis is one of the two most common complications of rubella and occurs in roughly 1 in 6,000 cases. This inflammation of the brain causes headaches, confusion, and seizures, and coma, long-term neurologic damage, and death can occur. The other common complication is thrombocytopenic purpura.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is a viral complication of rubella, not a bacterial meningitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Encephalitis is the right diagnosis but far rarer than 1 in 50 cases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myocarditis is described among congenital rubella findings and would not explain seizures.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytopenic purpura causes bleeding from low platelets, not seizures and confusion.

questions.stem: An infant is born to a woman who had a febrile rash illness during the first trimester while living in a country where rubella remains endemic. Which of the following is the classic triad of congenital rubella syndrome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cataracts, deafness, and cardiac malformations

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, and pneumonia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microcephaly, chorioretinitis, and periventricular calcifications

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recurrent infections, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seizures, hearing loss, and vesicular skin lesions

explanation.summary: The classic triad of congenital rubella syndrome is cataracts, deafness, and congenital heart defects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rubella is a TORCH pathogen, and infection during pregnancy can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, or severe congenital disease. Infants born with congenital rubella syndrome can have a broad range of findings, but the classic triad is cataracts, deafness, and congenital heart defects. Roughly 100,000 children are born with CRS each year worldwide.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These are additional possible findings in CRS but are not the classic triad.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This combination describes congenital cytomegalovirus rather than congenital rubella.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recurrent infections and chronic diarrhea describe the neonatal presentation of congenital HIV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vesicular skin lesions and meningoencephalitis point to congenital herpes simplex.

questions.stem: A newborn with congenital rubella syndrome has scattered purple-red papules over the trunk that the attending describes as blueberry muffin lesions. The platelet count is 42,000/mm3. These skin findings represent which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Granulomas formed around deposited viral antigen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemangiomas induced by prolonged intrauterine hypoxia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Petechiae and purpura resulting from thrombocytopenia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Septic emboli arising from infected cardiac vegetations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesicles produced by viral replication within the epidermis

explanation.summary: The blueberry muffin rash of congenital rubella consists of petechiae and purpura, and thrombocytopenia is one of the accompanying findings.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond the classic triad, infants with congenital rubella syndrome may have petechiae and purpura described as blueberry muffin lesions, together with thrombocytopenia, anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, hepatitis with possible jaundice, diarrhea, pneumonia, myocarditis, and lymphadenopathy. A blueberry muffin rash can also appear in congenital cytomegalovirus, which is one reason the two are confused.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granuloma formation does not describe the blueberry muffin rash.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blueberry muffin lesions are petechial and purpuric, not vascular tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Congenital heart disease in CRS is structural, and these lesions are not embolic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vesicular lesions are the hallmark of congenital herpes simplex rather than rubella.

questions.stem: A newborn has a blueberry muffin rash and fails the newborn hearing screen. Head CT shows periventricular calcifications, the head circumference is below the third percentile, and funduscopic examination shows chorioretinitis. The lenses are clear. Which of the following is the most likely congenital infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Congenital cytomegalovirus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Congenital herpes simplex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congenital HIV

choices.label: D
choices.text: Congenital rubella

choices.label: E
choices.text: Congenital Zika

explanation.summary: Chorioretinitis with microcephaly and periventricular calcifications separates congenital CMV from congenital rubella, which causes cataracts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congenital rubella and congenital cytomegalovirus overlap in that both cause hearing loss and a blueberry muffin rash, which is why they are commonly confused. The eye findings distinguish them: rubella causes cataracts, while CMV causes chorioretinitis, inflammation of the choroid and retina. CMV also causes microcephaly and periventricular calcifications, whereas congenital heart defects belong to rubella.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Congenital herpes simplex causes meningoencephalitis and vesicular lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Congenital HIV presents with recurrent infections and chronic diarrhea in the neonate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Congenital rubella would be expected to produce cataracts and a congenital heart defect, not chorioretinitis with periventricular calcifications.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika can cause microcephaly, but it does not account for the chorioretinitis and periventricular calcifications seen here.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman who is planning a pregnancy has no record of childhood vaccination and no current symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to determine whether she is immune to rubella?

choices.label: A
choices.text: RT-PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab for rubella virus

choices.label: B
choices.text: RT-PCR of a stool specimen

choices.label: C
choices.text: RT-PCR of a urine specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum IgG titer against rubella virus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viral culture of a throat swab

explanation.summary: Rubella immunity is assessed with IgG titers, while RT-PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab is used to detect active infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rubella immunity is assessed by determining IgG titers against the virus. Titers are specifically performed in people without knowledge of their vaccination status or in those who might become pregnant, exactly this patient's situation. Detecting the virus itself is a different question, answered by RT-PCR.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nasopharyngeal RT-PCR is the preferred way to detect active rubella infection, not to assess immunity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Stool testing is used for the enteric viruses in this brick, not for rubella immunity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urine is an acceptable specimen for detecting virus, but it does not measure immune status.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Culture does not address whether she has protective antibody.
